records.name_note: NC State's page title parenthetical lists Common Cypress, Italian Cypress, Mediterranean Cypress in alphabetical order, and its Common Name(s) list renders the same three names in the same order, so Common Cypress comes first; NC State's Description opens with Italian cypress. RHS's dedicated page title pairs the binomial with Italian cypress, and its Other common names line reads Mediterranean cypress. Italian Cypress is used as the common name because RHS's title and NC State's Description both lead with it.
unknowns: Two admissible dedicated pages were read: NC State and RHS (plant 5079). UF/IFAS EDIS (410), Clemson HGIC (403) and MoBot PlantFinder (fetch failure) were not read. RHS agrees on full sun, moist but well-drained soil and a height over 12 metres, but its Max Spread is 2.5-4 metres (about 98-157 in), much wider than NC State's 3-6 ft Dimensions width; NC State notes that commercially available forms are more columnar than wild plants.
toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail left null: neither NC State nor RHS carries a toxicity field for this species or mentions cats or dogs, and no cat/dog-naming admissible source was found.

is_houseplant is false: no admissible source frames this species as a houseplant. NC State files it as a Tree for USDA zones 7a-10b (40-70 ft. tall) and does not address indoor culture; RHS gives no indoor framing.

Size comes only from the species Dimensions block; the page notes commercially available forms are more columnar than wild plants, and cultivar entries ('Stricta', 'Swane's Golden', 'Tiny Tower', etc.) were not used.
soil_ph_min/max left null: the page lists all three bands (Acid (<6.0), Alkaline (>8.0), Neutral (6.0-8.0)), and the Acid and Alkaline bands are open-ended.

water_regime and water-interval fields left null: the page gives only a drought-tolerance trait and says young plants should receive adequate watering until established, with no watering regime; the #dry soils tolerant and #sandy soils tolerant tags are tolerances, not a sharp-drainage requirement.
humidity_need left null: the #humidity tolerant tag and Humidity under Resistance To Challenges are tolerances, not a need.
attracts_pollinators left null: NC State carries no Attracts field and tags the plant #wind pollinated.
is_edible left null: NC State addresses essential oils for soaps and perfume and wood for furniture, not eating.
chill_damage_f and all temperature fields left null: NC State gives only USDA zones 7a-10b, a hardiness range, not a damage-onset temperature.
direct_sun_hours_max left null: the page's Light field gives only a minimum ('6 or more hours'), no maximum.
fertilize fields left null: no fertilizing guidance on the page.

records.name_note: NC State's page-title parenthetical lists Bluebeard first, then Blue Mist Shrub and Blue Spirea, and its prose opener uses "Blue spirea"; RHS's page title gives "bluebeard". Bluebeard is the name led by both dedicated hybrid pages. The ASCII "x" in NC State's name is normalised to the hybrid sign. Parent-species and cultivar pages were not used.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail left null: NC State's page for this hybrid carries no toxicity data and no admissible source found names cats or dogs.
is_edible left null: no admissible source addresses eating this plant.
is_houseplant is false: both dedicated pages treat it as an outdoor garden shrub (NC State Plant Type Shrub, USDA zones 6a-9b; RHS Position Full sun) and neither says anything about indoor culture.

No dedicated Missouri Botanical Garden page for the hybrid itself was found (only cultivar pages, which are unusable), and no dedicated Clemson, UF/IFAS, Penn State, UMD or UGA page for this exact hybrid was found. The only dedicated pages are NC State and RHS.

soil_drainage is moderate: NC State gives only a lone Good Drainage value, and its prose says loose, well-drained loamy soil. NC State also warns that crown rot may occur in poorly drained soils; that is a cultivation note, not a sharp-drainage requirement.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: RHS lists the pH as Acid or Alkaline or Neutral with no numeric bounds, and NC State gives no pH.

water_regime and the day-interval and dry-down fields left null: neither dedicated page states a watering instruction. NC State's 'tolerant of drought' and RHS's Drought Resistance are tolerance traits, not watering statements.
fertilize fields left null: NC State only says too much fertilizer will result in lanky growth, with no interval, months or strength.

Temperature, humidity and light-intensity fields and chill_damage_f left null: no onset temperature is given. NC State's zones 6a-9b and RHS's H4 are hardiness ratings, not damage-onset figures. NC State says stems die back to the ground in cold climates below zone 6.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: the species prose gives no hour figure; NC State's '6 or more hours' is the generic category definition attached to its Light field value 'Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)', which defines a sun category and sets no species ceiling (the same correction the audit made on American Beautyberry).

Size: NC State's Dimensions block (2-3 ft height and width, converted to 24-36 in) is used. RHS gives Max Height 0.5-1 metres (19.7-39.4 in) and Max Spread 1-1.5 metres (39.4-59.1 in) over 5-10 years, so RHS spread is larger than NC State's. NC State's cultivar 'Longwood Blue' 4 ft figure is a cultivar size and was not used.
outdoor_sun_exposure: both NC State (Full sun) and RHS (Full sun) agree.
RHS lists Drought Resistance as Yes and Moisture as Well-drained, and the NC State Insects, Diseases section notes no serious problems.

records.name_note: Admissible sources split on the lead common name. NC State has a dedicated page for Lycoris squamigera whose page-title parenthetical lists seven names in alphabetical order (Magic Lily, Mystery Lily, Naked Ladies, Resurrection Lily, Sesame Lily, Surprise Lily, Upstart), and whose prose calls the plant "the surprise lily"; Surprise Lily was chosen as the primary name because its prose uses it. MoBot's dedicated page gives its Common Name field as "Resurrection lily", and its Noteworthy Characteristics prose mentions surprise lily only as a genus-level nickname for Lycoris ("Plants in the genus Lycoris are sometimes commonly called resurrection flower, surprise lily or magic lily"). RHS's dedicated profile leads with "Resurrection lily" and lists only magic lily, mystery lily, sesame lily and upstart as other common names, so two of the three admissible sources lead with Resurrection lily. NC State lists Amaryliis hallii, Hippeastrum squamigerum and Lycoris x squamigera under "Previously known as", but its own page title and H1 use the bare binomial Lycoris squamigera, so the name is recorded without a hybrid sign. RHS gives the Name Status as Unresolved for this page.
records.toxicity_detail: Source: NC State Plant Toolbox, Lycoris squamigera page. Its Poison block is scoped to humans (Problems tag "Poisonous to Humans"; Poison Severity: Low). Poison Symptoms: "CAUSES ONLY LOW TOXICITY IF EATEN. Abdominal pain, salivation, shivering, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea." Poison Toxic Principle: Lycorine, an alkaloid. Poison Part: Roots. Causes Contact Dermatitis: No. The Plant Type field lists three values: Bulb, Herbaceous Perennial, Poisonous. The page's tag list includes #poisonous. The page also carries a short line saying the plant has low severity poison characteristics. No admissible source names cats or dogs for this species, and NC State carries no Problem-for-Cats or Problem-for-Dogs tag, so toxic_to_pets is left null. NC State carries no separate handling warning. MoBot's page lists no toxicity information.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets left null: no admissible source names cats or dogs for Lycoris squamigera; NC State's Poison block is human-scoped only.

is_houseplant is false: no admissible source frames this as a houseplant; NC State files it as a hardy bulb and herbaceous perennial for USDA zones 5a-9a, best incorporated in a mixed ground cover or flowerbed.

water_regime left null: NC State prose says to water 'sparingly during the rest period and moderately during their growing season' and MoBot gives a structured 'Water: Medium' (mid-scale, disclosed as a counterpoint, not keep_moist); none maps cleanly to a single enum token. water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm and the day-interval fields are null for an in-ground bulb.

soil_ph_min left null: NC State's 'Acid (<6.0)' band is open-ended. soil_ph_max 8.0 is the closed top of NC State's 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' band; NC State does not tag Alkaline, and RHS's profile for this plant carries no pH field to check it against.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: the species prose gives no hour figure; NC State's '6 or more hours' is the generic category definition attached to its Light field value 'Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)', which defines a sun category and sets no species ceiling (the same correction the audit made on American Beautyberry).
is_edible set false only on NC State's human-scoped poison data (low severity, roots, symptoms if eaten); no admissible source says whether any part is used for food.
chill_damage_f 28 comes from NC State prose about the bulbs; NC State's USDA zones 5a-9a and MoBot's zone 5-9 are hardiness ratings, not used as an onset figure.

name: sources split on the lead common name (NC State prose Surprise Lily vs MoBot and RHS Resurrection lily); RHS Name Status is Unresolved and WCVP is not an admissible source, so accepted-name status beyond NC State's bare binomial title is not confirmed here.

Not captured: temperatures, humidity, light in foot-candles, fertilizer, and the Hippeastrum squamigerum / Lycoris x squamigera synonymy details beyond NC State's former-names list. Clemson, UF/IFAS, Penn State, UMD and UGA were not found to carry a dedicated Lycoris squamigera page (Clemson refused automated fetches).

The three MoBot citations this record carries ('Resurrection lily' from the Common Name field, the genus-nickname sentence, and 'Full sun to part shade') cannot be checked from this machine: MoBot's server refuses the connection, so verify_quotes skips them. The auditor read all three verbatim on MoBot's live page (taxonid 275706) on 2026-10-09, and also saw that MoBot's longer common-names list exists only in an unquotable hover popup. No MoBot citation was added at landing.

records.name_note: NC State's dedicated Crocus sativus page is headed with the binomial Crocus sativus. Its Common Name(s) list reads Autumn Crocus, Saffron, Saffron Crocus; the list is alphabetized, and the browser page-title parenthetical gives the same three names in the same order. Autumn Crocus, the list's first entry, is already this catalog's common name for Colchicum autumnale, the plant NC State's is-often-confused-with module names for this species, so this record lands as Saffron Crocus, the name RHS's dedicated Crocus sativus page leads with (page title 'Crocus sativus | saffron crocus'). NC State lists Crocus autumnalis, Crocus officinalis and Crocus sativus var. officinalis under Previously known as.
records.toxicity_detail: Edibility is the stigmas only: NC State says "To harvest the saffron, remove the bright orange stigmas and use fresh or dry and store in air-tight containers for later use." and RHS says "Pick stigmas for drying as a flavouring and food colourant (saffron)." RHS's Potentially harmful field reads in full: "Ornamental bulbs - not to be eaten. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling. Pets: Ornamental bulbs - not to be eaten - see the HTA guide to potentially harmful plants for further information and useful contact numbers". RHS's Pets line names no animal, and NC State carries no Poison block and no Problem for Cats or Problem for Dogs tag for this species, so toxic_to_pets is left null. Nothing here is drawn from Colchicum autumnale (autumn crocus), the different plant NC State's is-often-confused-with module names.
unknowns: is_edible is true for the orange stigmas only, the spice: NC State says to harvest them and 'use fresh or dry and store in air-tight containers for later use', and RHS says 'Pick stigmas for drying as a flavouring and food colourant (saffron).' RHS's Potentially harmful field says the bulbs (the corms) are 'not to be eaten' and to wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling; its 'Pets:' line names no animal, so toxic_to_pets stays null. NC State has no Poison block and no Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tags. Nothing was imported from the Colchicum autumnale record.

soil_drainage left null: the page's Soil Drainage field shows Good Drainage and Occasionally Dry only (no Moist tag), and the prose says 'well-drained soil with moderate levels of organic matter' and warns of root rot 'if planted in a wet location'. That is not sharp/sandy drainage (fast) and does not meet the moderate criteria, so it is not forced into an enum.
Missouri Botanical Garden's Plant Finder page for Crocus sativus could not be loaded; RHS's dedicated page (plants/4929/crocus-sativus) was used alongside NC State.

water_regime, humidity, temperature, light_fc, fertilizer: neither NC State nor RHS states them for this species (RHS gives hardiness rating H6, a survival rating, not a damage-onset temperature). Soil pH: NC State gives none; RHS gives pH 'Alkaline or Neutral', a band with no numbers, so soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max stay null. RHS's Moisture field reads Well-drained. attracts_pollinators stays null: NC State says nothing, and RHS's 'Plants for pollinators' badge renders only as image alt text, not quotable rendered text. Size: RHS's Max Height is 'Up to 10 cm' (about 3.9 in) and Max Spread 0-0.1 metre (about 0-3.9 in), lower than NC State's 6-10 in height; NC State's Dimensions block is used.
direct_sun_hours_max left null: the '6 or more hours' wording is NC State's generic Light category label, not species-specific prose.

records.name_note: NC State's Common Name(s) list is alphabetized (Regal Lily, Royal Lily, Trumpet Lily) and its order matches the page-title parenthetical; RHS's page title gives "regal lily" and lists "king's lily, royal lily" as other common names. 'Trumpet Lily' also names the Trumpet/Aurelian hybrid group and appears on NC State's L. longiflorum page, so nothing was taken from those records.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's poison banner reads 'This plant has medium severity poison characteristics.'; its Poisonous to Humans block (human-scoped) gives Poison Severity: Medium; Poison Symptoms: Excessive drooling, vomiting, loss of appetite; Poison Toxic Principle: unknown; Causes Contact Dermatitis: No; Poison Part: Flowers, Fruits, Leaves, Seeds, Stems (bulb not listed). NC State Problems: Poisonous to Humans, Problem for Cats, Problem for Children (no dog tag); Plant Type: Bulb, Herbaceous Perennial, Poisonous. NC State prose: 'The plant is toxic to cats and can be fatal.' RHS: 'Ornamental bulbs - not to be eaten. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling. TOXIC to pets if eaten (cats)'. Sources differ on handling (RHS advises gloves; NC State says it does not cause contact dermatitis) and on the bulb (RHS says not to be eaten; NC State does not list it as a poison part). No source names dogs.
unknowns: Missouri Botanical Garden's Lilium regale page (plantfinder.mobot.org taxonid=281788) could not be loaded in this session (TLS/proxy error), so nothing is drawn from it. No Clemson HGIC, UF/IFAS, Penn State, UMD or UGA page dedicated to Lilium regale was found; only NC State and RHS are cited.

is_houseplant is false: no admissible source addresses indoor culture; NC State lists it as a hardy bulb and herbaceous perennial for USDA zones 4a-8b that can also be grown in 3-gallon containers (an outdoor use), and RHS suggests flower borders and beds.

water_regime and the water_* fields left null: NC State's 'drought-tolerant and flourishes with good moisture year-round' is a preference/tolerance trait, not a watering instruction; 'plant the bulbs in raised beds' in hot humid areas is siting advice and is not read as a fast-drainage signal. No dry-down or interval figures are stated.

soil_drainage moderate rests on RHS Moisture 'Moist but well-drained or Well-drained' plus NC State's Good Drainage and 'well-drained' soil prose; NC State's Soil Drainage field is only 'Good Drainage' and carries no moisture pair.

soil_ph_min left null because NC State's Acid (<6.0) band is open-ended; soil_ph_max 8.0 is the closed top of NC State's Neutral (6.0-8.0) band and RHS pH lists only Acid or Neutral, though RHS Soil Types also includes Chalk.

outdoor_sun_exposure is full_sun only: RHS Position lists only Full sun; NC State's Light field also lists Partial Shade, but its tags call the plant '#partial shade tolerant', so part shade is a tolerance and is not listed. direct_sun_hours_max left null: NC State's hour figures are the generic category definitions attached to its Light values, and no species prose gives a maximum.

is_edible false rests on RHS's 'not to be eaten' for ornamental bulbs; NC State lists Fruits, Seeds, Leaves, Stems, Flowers as poison parts but its Poison Toxic Principle is unknown and it does not list bulbs/roots as a poison part, while its prose says rodents, deer and rabbits eat the bulb.

toxic_to_pets true is cat-scoped only, on this species' own pages: NC State's Problem for Cats value and its prose 'The plant is toxic to cats and can be fatal.', and RHS's 'TOXIC to pets if eaten (cats)'. No source names dogs for this species, and no genus-level lily warning is used. NC State's Poison block (Medium severity, symptoms, parts) is human-scoped.

Temperature, humidity, light (fc), fertilizing and chill-damage fields are null: no admissible source states them for this species (hardiness zones 4a-8b and RHS H6 are survival ratings, not damage onsets).

RHS's Size section gives Max Height 1-1.5 metres and Max Spread 0.1-0.5 metres (about 39-59 in and 4-20 in), narrower than NC State's 3-6 ft by 9-24 in, though RHS's description reads 'A vigorous bulbous perennial to 2m in height'; NC State, the anchor source, is used.

unknowns: Only NC State's Agave amica page loaded. RHS (polianthes-tuberosa URLs returned 404), MoBot and the other admissible hosts gave no usable dedicated page (plantfinder.mobot.org was sandbox-denied), so all fields rest on a single source.

WCVP/POWO status could not be checked from admissible sources; scientific_name_accepted follows NC State's current heading Agave amica, with Polianthes tuberosa recorded as the former name NC State lists under Previously known as.
toxic_to_pets, toxicity_detail left null: NC State's page has no Poison block and no Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tag; no admissible source naming this species for cats or dogs was found.
is_edible left null: NC State's only use statement is perfume (flowers 'used to make perfumes', Extracts used to make perfume); that is not an edibility claim.

is_houseplant is false: NC State describes in-ground culture (USDA zones 8a-10b) and says to lift tubers and store them inside in zones lower than 8 or grow them in pots and bring them inside for the winter; that is overwintering, not houseplant culture, and no admissible source frames it as a houseplant.

soil_drainage null: NC State's structured Soil Drainage field reads Good Drainage and Occasionally Dry (no Moist or Occasionally Wet tag), and its prose asks for well-drained loamy or sandy soil and warns that too-wet soils cause root rot; that matches neither the catalog's moderate (moist but well-drained) nor its fast (sharp/sandy) definition, so the field is left null.
soil_ph_max null: NC State gives only the closed band Neutral (6.0-8.0) and no RHS pH field was available to check the ceiling; soil_ph_min 6.0 is the floor of that band.
direct_sun_hours_max null: the 6+ hours and 2-6 hours figures appear in NC State's Light category labels, not species-specific prose.
outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's Light field lists Full sun and Partial Shade; Partial Shade is mapped to part_shade.

water_regime dry_surface_between is read from 'allow the soil to partially dry between watering'; no dry-down depth or day interval is stated, so those fields are null. Watering is reduced once leaves yellow and the plant goes dormant, but no numeric dormant interval is given.
chill_damage_f null: NC State gives zones 8a-10b and a bulb-storage temperature of 70-75 F, neither a damage-onset temperature; it advises lifting tubers in zones lower than 8.
Temperature, humidity, light footcandle, fertilizer fields are null: not stated by NC State.
Spread range 12-42 in comes from NC State's Width 1 ft. 0 in. - 3 ft. 6 in.; its Description separately says the plant grows 2-3 feet tall.
